output_json.patch_notes: Root-cause fix in Expand.extractFile(): after resolving the zip entry's target File via FileUtils.resolveFile(dir, entryName), verify f.getCanonicalPath() starts with dir.getCanonicalPath() + File.separator before doing anything else (mkdirs on parent, mkdirs on f itself for directory entries, FileOutputStream write, or setLastModified). If the check fails, an IOException is thrown describing the offending entry name; this propagates through extractFile's `throws Exception` and is caught/wrapped by expandFile's existing `catch (IOException ioe)` handler, so callers see a clean Exception instead of a partially-completed malicious extraction. Added ExpandTest.java with two regression tests: one builds a zip with a "../evil.txt" entry and asserts Expand.execute() throws and no file is written outside the destination directory; the other builds a normal nested-path zip entry and asserts it still extracts correctly into the destination, proving benign behavior is preserved.
output_json.risk_notes: Low risk. The check only rejects entries whose resolved path would escape the destination directory — normal relative entries (including nested subdirectories) continue to resolve inside dir and are unaffected, as confirmed by the full test suite (302 tests, 0 failures) and a successful `mvn package`. Uses canonical paths (resolves symlinks/`..`/`.`) consistent with how FileUtils.resolveFile already canonicalizes absolute paths, and appends File.separator to the directory boundary to avoid a same-prefix sibling-directory bypass (e.g. "/dest-evil" vs "/dest"). No API signature changes; behavior change is limited to throwing on genuinely malicious entries.
output_json.summary: Fixed a Zip Slip / path traversal (CWE-22) vulnerability in org.codehaus.plexus.util.Expand#extractFile. Zip entry names read via ZipEntry.getName() were passed unvalidated through FileUtils.resolveFile() to build the destination file path used for directory creation (Expand.java:164), file creation via FileOutputStream (Expand.java:178), and setLastModified (Expand.java:204). A crafted zip entry name (e.g. "../../etc/passwd" or an absolute path) could resolve outside the intended destination directory, letting a malicious archive write/overwrite arbitrary files on extraction. The fix adds a single root-cause check right after the entry's target File is resolved: the resolved file's canonical path must be contained within the destination directory's canonical path (with a trailing separator to prevent sibling-directory prefix bypass, e.g. "/dest-evil" matching "/dest"). If not, extraction throws before any directory creation, file write, or mtime modification occurs — covering all three previously-vulnerable sink operations in one place, including relative traversal, absolute-path entries, and mixed-separator variants (since FileUtils.resolveFile already normalizes separators and canonicalizes absolute paths before our check runs).
